requirements.evidence: The contract is implemented: `CreateQueue`/`UpdateQueue` validate name and slug and handle per-entity uniqueness (`app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:17-41`, `app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:19-66`), `SetQueueAccess` upserts/revokes with the audit log (`app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:30-118`), `QueuePolicy` exposes `create`, `update`, `manageAccess`, `call` (`app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:17-74`), and both call paths authorize after the inactive check (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:104-111`). Edge cases remain: an explicitly blank slug is treated as omitted (`app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:22-24`), and the DB-race conversion only recognizes MySQL/SQLite unique errors (`app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:66-73`).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through actions (`app/Actions/CreateQueue.php`, `app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php`, `app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php`), authorization lives in a policy, the migration is reversible with FKs, cascade deletes and the composite unique index (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_120000_create_queue_access_table.php:14-29`), `QueueAccess` declares fillable attributes (`app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11`), and the requested docs/CHANGELOG are updated (`docs/business-rules.md:101-122`, `docs/database-schema.md`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`).

security.evidence: Every action authorizes before writing (`app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:19`, `app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:26`, `app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:30`), both call paths check the `call` ability (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:108`), permissions are validated against a string allow-list (`app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:47-60`), and the policy denies non-members, ungranted employees, grants on other queues, and corrupted non-array permissions (`app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:42-65`).

tests.evidence: The new suite covers lifecycle, name/slug validation, duplicate slugs within and across entities, authorization denials, every update combination, deactivation preserving tickets, audit grant/revoke/no-op, invalid and cross-entity grants, self-grant denial, all policy abilities, corrupted permissions, all `CallMode` authorization paths, the `Ticket::call` order, and factory entity consistency (`tests/QueueManagementTest.php:34-303`). Existing `CallNextTicket` tests were updated rather than weakened (`tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php`, `tests/Pest.php:54-66`).

simplicity.evidence: Queue attribute validation is shared in a trait, but `SetQueueAccess` re-implements the same unique-violation helper (`app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:111-118` versus `app/Actions/Concerns/ValidatesQueueAttributes.php:66-73`), and the factory uses two coupled closures (`database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:24-41`) where a small helper would be easier to follow.

readability.evidence: Names are descriptive and methods are small; comments explain the lock/authorization order (`app/Models/Ticket.php:90-97`, `app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:33-35`) and the docs summarize the abilities and invariants (`docs/business-rules.md:101-122`).

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the requested domain/authorization slice: actions, policy, migration/model/factory, tests, and the three requested docs. No UI, queue deletion, plan limits, or extra permissions were added.

issues.explanation: The unique-violation detector only treats SQLSTATE 23000 and the strings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate' as races; PostgreSQL reports 23505 with a lowercase 'duplicate key value', so on PostgreSQL a DB unique-index race would still surface as a raw QueryException instead of the required ValidationException.

An explicitly supplied blank or whitespace-only slug is silently treated as omitted and replaced with the name slug, while `UpdateQueue` rejects an empty slug through `normalizeSlug()`; the two actions should handle this edge case consistently.
The private `isUniqueViolation()` copies the identical helper from the `ValidatesQueueAttributes` trait, leaving the DB-specific matching logic in two places to maintain.
Calling `UpdateQueue` with `name`, `slug` and `isActive` all null still opens a transaction, locks and saves the queue, bumping `updated_at`; a no-op update could return early without writing.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, per-queue access grants/policy, call authorization on both call paths, and comprehensive tests plus the requested documentation. It is well scoped and secure; the remaining concerns are minor: DB-specific race handling that misses PostgreSQL, an inconsistent blank-slug edge case, and a duplicated unique-violation helper.
